idea-plugin.name: Laravel API
idea-plugin.description:
IDE support for dskripchenko/laravel-api — the docblock markup its OpenAPI generator reads, and the route map its getMethods() declares.

The package fails quietly by design, and that is what this plugin is for. An action whose controller method was renamed answers 404 — the same 404 as a mistyped URL, so nothing in the logs tells the two apart. A type outside the known set silently becomes string. A @response 200 {UserResponse} naming a template nobody declared becomes a $ref pointing at nothing, in a spec that still passes validation. In every one of those cases the application boots, the tests pass, and the mistake reaches whoever consumes the API.

Running the package's own api:lint over one real application turned up 1204 such references at once — a couple of dozen causes, multiplied by every resource and every panel. This plugin shows the same thing while typing, and can run that command for you besides.

While you type

  • Highlights the markup — @input, @output, @header, @response, @security, @default, @example. Types, formats, variables, template references and status codes are coloured, so a line the generator has stopped understanding stops looking like the ones it still does.
  • Reports markup that does not parse, where it is written. The generator drops such a line without a word and the field never reaches the spec.
  • Flags unknown types with the consequence named: the generator will call the field string.
  • Compares the markup against the validation rules. A field the method validates and the docblock never mentions is reported on the rule itself, with a quick fix that writes the tag from it — email becomes string(email), a rule that is not required becomes an optional field, in:a,b becomes an enumeration. The description stays for a person to write.
  • Marks dangling references — a template or a security scheme nothing declares — and offers a quick fix that declares the template for you, creating getOpenApiTemplates() when the class has none, with the name taken verbatim from the docblock.
  • Turns the silent 404 red: an action pointing at a missing, non-public or static method is an error while you type, not a bug report later — and a quick fix writes that method, placed and shaped like the ones already in the class.
  • Completes types, formats, template names, security schemes and status codes — and, deliberately, nothing at all once the caret has passed the variable into the description.

Getting around

  • Navigates from {TemplateName}, @Model, @security Scheme and @input [method] to their declarations.
  • Finds usages of a response template — every docblock naming it, through the usual Find Usages, plus a gutter arrow from the declaration to them. A template read only by the generator otherwise looks unused to the IDE.
  • Draws gutter arrows both ways between the route map and the controllers: from an action's key to the method it routes, and from a method back to every action routing it. An action with no arrow points at a method that is not there.
  • Lists every endpoint the route map declares in a tool window — controller, action, method, searchable, and a double-click opens the code. The map is spread across classes by design; this is the one place it can be read whole.

On demand

  • Runs api:lint from the IDE and makes its findings clickable. The command carries far more rules than an editor can afford to evaluate on every keystroke — asking the application is cheaper than writing them twice.

Quiet by default

Nothing fires unless the project actually has the package on its classpath: @input and @output are ordinary words elsewhere. And @security is not policed while a project declares no schemes at all — such an application has evidently not taken the feature up, and painting every tag red would teach people to look past the plugin rather than at it. Rules assembled at runtime — from a variable, a merge, a Rule::when — are read by nobody here: a half-read array would report fields that are documented three lines further up.

Every check is an ordinary inspection, so severity, suppression and the off switch are where you already look for them — Settings | Editor | Inspections, under Laravel API. The plugin has no settings screen of its own.

Requirements

PhpStorm, or IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate with the PHP plugin installed. The whole plugin hangs off the PHP plugin's PSI, so IDEA Community cannot run it — JetBrains does not publish the PHP plugin for it.
